original.target_description: Study 1 observational bar sample: blood alcohol concentration and footbridge utilitarian response; no placebo or administered-dose condition.

replication.target_description: Single preregistered experiment; traditional switch and footbridge trolley judgments. Alcohol sample receiving 1.6 grams of alcohol at 40% strength per kg body weight located, but locator does not identify a unique condition-specific test or comparator.

n.sample_role: participants in the alcohol condition of the final analytic sample
n.exclusions: 58 participants excluded from analyses for failing one or more attention checks; final sample 329.
n.quote:
106 participants
were in alcohol condition (53 women, 53 men)

reported_success.quote: Despite these improvements, we failed to obtain any significant effect of alcohol on moral judgments.

notes:
Original primary-source acquisition terminal miss: /home/lukas/.t3/worktrees/fred-data/audit-fred-stats-2026-10/audit/fred_stats_2026-10/texts/d4bab9fd3fd7870a67e4d390.miss. Original statistics quoted in the replication were not substituted for the unavailable original. The specified condition and its post-exclusion sample count are printed, but no unique condition-specific inferential test is established by the neutral description and p. 7 locator. The printed omnibus Alcohol Group result pools all three conditions and both trolley dilemmas; it is not assigned to this single-condition target. Effect size and p remain null; target_match remains unknown. Authors’ reported-success verdict concerns the overall alcohol/moral-judgment hypothesis.
Source follow-up: Requested placebo condition or fixed administered alcohol dose is absent from this original field study; participants were recruited at a bar and BAC measured. Known sample/design mismatch; no condition-specific statistics extracted.
